text: What will be the projection of vector $\vec{A}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ on vector $\vec{B}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ ?

$=\frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}).(\hat{i}+\hat{j})}{\sqrt{2}}\frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j})}{\sqrt{2}}$

$=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\times\frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j})}{\sqrt{2}}$

$=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$

text: A body is projected vertically upwards from the surface of earth with a velocity sufficient enough to carry it to infinity. The time taken by it to reach height h is $___________ s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}-\frac{GMm}{r}=0\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{r}}$

$\frac{dr}{dt}=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{r}}$

$\Rightarrow \int\limits _{R_{e}}^{(R_{e}+h)}\sqrt{r}dr=\int\limits _{0}^{t}\sqrt{2GM}dt$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}\left [(R_{e}+h)^{3/2}-R_{e}^{3/2}\right ]=(t)\sqrt{2GM}$

$\Rightarrow t=\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2R_{e}}{g}}\left [\left (1+\frac{h}{R_{e}}\right )^{\frac{3}{2}}-1\right ]$

text: An electric dipole is placed on x-axis in proximity to a line charge of linear charge density 3.0 $\times$ $10^{-6} C/m$. Line charge is placed on z-axis and positive and negative charge of dipole is at a distance of 10 mm and 12 mm from the origin respectively. If total force of 4N is exerted on the dipole, find out the amount of positive or negative charge of the dipole.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The line charge produces a radial field $E=\dfrac{2kλ}{r}$. The $+q$ charge at $r_{1}=10\text{mm}$ is pushed away from the line and the $-q$ charge at $r_{2}=12\text{mm}$ is pulled towards it.


[IMG]

$F=2kλq\left (\dfrac{1}{r_{1}}-\dfrac{1}{r_{2}}\right )=2kλq\dfrac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{r_{1}r_{2}}$

$\dfrac{r_{2}-r_{1}}{r_{1}r_{2}}=\dfrac{2\times 10^{-3}}{(10\times 10^{-3})(12\times 10^{-3})}=\dfrac{50}{3}\text{m}^{-1}$

$4=2\times 9\times 10^{9}\times 3\times 10^{-6}\times \dfrac{50}{3}\times q=9\times 10^{5}q$

$q=\dfrac{4}{9\times 10^{5}}=4.44\times 10^{-6}\text{C}=4.44μ\text{C}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Match List - I with List - II

  
    
    List - I
    
    List - II
  

  
    (a)
    $ωL>\frac{1}{ωC}$
    (i)
    Current is in phase with emf
  
  
    (b)
    $ωL=\frac{1}{ωC}$
    (ii)
    Current lags behind the applied emf
  
  
    (c)
    $ωL<\frac{1}{ωC}$
    (iii)
    Maximum current occurs
  
  
    (d)
    Resonant frequency
    (iv)
    Current leads the emf
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the circuit contain a resistance $R$, an inductance $L$ and a capacitance $C$ connected in series.


[IMG]


The inductive reactance is $X_{L}=ωL$ and the capacitive reactance is $X_{C}=\dfrac{1}{ωC}$.

Let an instantaneous sinusoidal current $i=i_{0}\sin (ωt)$ flow through the series $L-C-R$ circuit. Because the resistor $R$, the inductor $L$ and the capacitor $C$ are in series, the same current $i$ flows through each of them at every instant.

Across the resistor $R$, by Ohm's law, $v_{R}=iR=i_{0}R\sin (ωt)=V_{R0}\sin (ωt)$, where $V_{R0}=i_{0}R$. Thus, $v_{R}$ is in phase with the current $i$.


[IMG]


Across the inductor $L$, by Faraday's law of self-induction, the potential difference across an ideal inductor is

$V_{L}=L\frac{di}{dt}=L\frac{d}{dt}(i_{0}\sin ωt)=i_{0}(ωL)\cos (ωt)=i_{0}X_{L}\sin \left (ωt+\frac{π}{2}\right )$


[IMG]


Here $X_{L}=ωL$ and $V_{L0}=i_{0}X_{L}$. Thus, $v_{L}$ leads the current $i$ by a phase angle $\dfrac{π}{2}$.

Across the capacitor $C$, the charge on its plates is $q=\int idt=-\dfrac{i_{0}}{ω}\cos (ωt)$, so the voltage across the capacitor at any time $t$ is

$V_{C}=\frac{q}{C}=-\frac{i_{0}}{ωC}\cos (ωt)=i_{0}X_{C}\sin \left (ωt-\frac{π}{2}\right )$


[IMG]


Here $X_{C}=\dfrac{1}{ωC}$ and $V_{C0}=i_{0}X_{C}$. Thus, $v_{C}$ lags behind the current $i$ by a phase angle $\dfrac{π}{2}$.

By Kirchhoff's loop rule, at every instant the applied emf $V$ equals the sum of the instantaneous voltages across the three elements, $V=V_{R}+V_{L}+V_{C}$.


[IMG]


The resultant peak applied emf $V_{0}$ is

$V_{0}=\sqrt{V_{R0}^{2}+(V_{L0}-V_{C0})^{2}}=i_{0}\sqrt{R^{2}+(X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}$

The total impedance $Z=\dfrac{V_{0}}{i_{0}}$ is

$Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+\left (ωL-\frac{1}{ωC}\right )^{2}}$

and the peak current in the circuit is

$i_{0}=\frac{V_{0}}{Z}=\frac{V_{0}}{⎷R^{2}+\left (ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}\right )^{2}}$

From the phasor triangle, the phase angle $𝜙$ by which the applied emf $V$ leads the current $i$ is given by

$\tan 𝜙=\frac{V_{L0}-V_{C0}}{V_{R0}}=\frac{i_{0}(X_{L}-X_{C})}{i_{0}R}=\frac{ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}}{R}$

So the applied emf is $V=V_{0}\sin (ωt+𝜙)$.

Case (a): $ωL>\dfrac{1}{ωC}(X_{L}>X_{C})$


[IMG]


Since $ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}>0$, the inductive reactance dominates the capacitive reactance and $\tan 𝜙>0$, which means the phase angle $𝜙$ is positive $\left (0<𝜙<\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$.

Because the applied emf $V=V_{0}\sin (ωt+𝜙)$ is ahead of the current $i=i_{0}\sin (ωt)$ by the positive phase $𝜙$, the current lags behind the applied emf. Therefore, (a) matches (ii).

Case (b): $ωL=\dfrac{1}{ωC}(X_{L}=X_{C})$

Since $ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}=0$, we have $\tan 𝜙=0\Rightarrow 𝜙=0$. With zero phase difference between the emf and the current, the current is in phase with the emf, matching (i).

The reactive term $\left (ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}\right )^{2}=0$, so the impedance $Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+0}=R$ takes its minimum possible value. Because $i_{0}=\dfrac{V_{0}}{Z}$, the minimum impedance gives the maximum current in the circuit, matching (iii).

Therefore, (b) matches (i), (iii).

Case (c): $ωL<\dfrac{1}{ωC}(X_{L}<X_{C})$


[IMG]


Since $ωL-\dfrac{1}{ωC}<0$, we have $\tan 𝜙<0$, which means the phase angle $𝜙$ is negative $\left (-\dfrac{π}{2}<𝜙<0\right )$.

Because the applied emf $V=V_{0}\sin (ωt-|𝜙|)$ lags behind the current $i=i_{0}\sin (ωt)$, the current leads the emf. Therefore, (c) matches (iv).

Case (d): Resonant frequency

Resonance in a series $L-C-R$ circuit occurs at the angular frequency $ω_{r}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, at which the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance $\left (ω_{r}L=\dfrac{1}{ω_{r}C}\right )$. So, as in case (b), the current is in phase with the emf (i) and the maximum current occurs (iii).

Therefore, (d) matches (i), (iii).

So (a)–(ii), (b)–(i), (c)–(iv) and (d)–(iii); (b) also gives the maximum current (iii) and (d) also has the current in phase with the emf (i), and among the given options only a(ii), b(i), c(iv), d(iii) agrees with these matches.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text: What will be the average value of energy for a monoatomic gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature T?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a monoatomic ideal gas, the average kinetic energy per molecule is determined by the equipartition theorem. This theorem states that the energy is equally distributed among all the available degrees of freedom.

A monoatomic gas has three translational degrees of freedom, corresponding to motion in the x, y, and z directions. Each degree of freedom contributes an average energy of $\frac{1}{2}k_{B}T$, where $k_{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

So for a monoatomic gas with three translational degrees of freedom, the average energy per molecule is: $\frac{3}{2}k_{B}T.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text:
Three students $S_{1}, S_{2}$ and $S_{3}$ perform an experiment for determining the acceleration due to gravity (g) using a simple pendulum. They use different lengths of pendulum and record time for different number of oscillations. The observations are as shown in the table.

  
    Student
No.
    Length of
Pendulum (cm)
    No. of
oscillations (n)
    Total time for
n oscillations
    Time
period (s)
  

  
    1
    64.0
    8
    128.0
    16.0
  
  
    2
    64.0
    4
    64.0
    16.0
  
  
    3
    20.0
    4
    36.0
    9.0
  

(Least count of length = 0.1 cm and Least count for time = 0.1 s)

If $E_{1}, E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$ are the percentage errors in 'g' for students 1, 2 and 3 respectively, then the minimum percentage error is obtained by student no. $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a simple pendulum $T=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$, so $g=\dfrac{4π^{2}l}{T^{2}}$ with $T=\dfrac{t}{n}$.

The number of oscillations $n$ is exact, so $\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}=\dfrac{\Delta t}{t}$ and the percentage error in $g$ is

$E=\left (\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}+2\dfrac{\Delta t}{t}\right )\times 100%,\Delta l=0.1\text{cm},\Delta t=0.1\text{s}$

For $S_{1}$ ($l=64.0\text{cm}$, $t=128.0\text{s}$):

$E_{1}=\left (\dfrac{0.1}{64.0}+\dfrac{2\times 0.1}{128.0}\right )\times 100%=\dfrac{20}{64}%\approx 0.31%$

For $S_{2}$ ($l=64.0\text{cm}$, $t=64.0\text{s}$):

$E_{2}=\left (\dfrac{0.1}{64.0}+\dfrac{2\times 0.1}{64.0}\right )\times 100%=\dfrac{30}{64}%\approx 0.47%$

For $S_{3}$ ($l=20.0\text{cm}$, $t=36.0\text{s}$):

$E_{3}=\left (\dfrac{0.1}{20.0}+\dfrac{2\times 0.1}{36.0}\right )\times 100%=\dfrac{19}{18}%\approx 1.06%$

$S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ use the same length and period, but $S_{1}$ times more oscillations, so its relative error in time is smaller. The minimum error is $E_{1}$.

Hence, the answer is 1.

text: Three particles P, Q and R are moving along the vectors $\vec{A}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}=\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{C}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ respectively. They strike on a point and start to move in different directions. Now particle P is moving normal to the plane which contains vector $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$. Similarly particle Q is moving normal to the plane which contains vector $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$. The angle between the direction of motion of P and Q is $\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right )$. Then the value of x is $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve the problem, we need to determine the vectors normal to the planes containing given vectors and find the angle between those normal vectors.

First, let's find the vectors normal to the plane containing vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$. The normal vector can be calculated using the cross product:

$\vec{A}\times \vec{B}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times (\hat{j}+\widehat{k})$.

Using the properties of the cross product:

$\begin{array}{ll} \vec{A}\times \vec{B} & =(\hat{i}\times \hat{j})+(\hat{i}\times \widehat{k})+(\hat{j}\times \hat{j})+(\hat{j}\times \widehat{k}) \\ =\widehat{k}-\hat{j}+0+\hat{i} \\ =\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}. \end{array}$

So, the vector normal to the plane containing vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is $\vec{N}_{1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$.

Next, let's find the vector normal to the plane containing vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$:

$\vec{A}\times \vec{C}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times (-\hat{i}+\hat{j})$.

Using the properties of the cross product:

$\begin{array}{ll} \vec{A}\times \vec{C} & =(\hat{i}\times -\hat{i})+(\hat{i}\times \hat{j})+(\hat{j}\times -\hat{i})+(\hat{j}\times \hat{j}) \\ =0+\widehat{k}+\widehat{k}+0 \\ =2\widehat{k}. \end{array}$

So, the vector normal to the plane containing vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{C}$ is $\vec{N}_{2}=2\widehat{k}$. But we just need the direction of this vector, not its magnitude, so we can simplify it to $\widehat{k}$.

Now, to find the angle between the two normal vectors $\vec{N}_{1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{N}_{2}=\widehat{k}$, we use the dot product formula:

$\cos (θ)=\frac{\vec{N}_{1}\cdot \vec{N}_{2}}{||\vec{N}_{1}||||\vec{N}_{2}||}$

First, calculate the dot product:

$\vec{N}_{1}\cdot \vec{N}_{2}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k})\cdot \widehat{k}=0+0+1=1$

Next, find the magnitude of the vectors:

$||\vec{N}_{1}||=\sqrt{1^{2}+(-1)^{2}+1^{2}}=\sqrt{3}$

$||\vec{N}_{2}||=\sqrt{0^{2}+0^{2}+1^{2}}=1$

Now substitute these into the cosine formula:

$\cos (θ)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}\times 1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}$

Therefore, $\cos ^{-1}(\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}})=\cos ^{-1}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})$ indicates $x=3$.

So, the value of $x$ is:

3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text:
The total charge enclosed in an incremental volume of 2 $\times$ $10^{-9} m^{3}$ located at the origin is $___________ nC$, if electric flux density of its field is found as

$D = e^{-x} \sin  y$ $\hat{i}$ $-$ $e^{-x} \cos  y$ $\hat{j}$ + 2z $\widehat{k}$ $C/m^{2}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$D–=ε_{0}E–$

$Div.\qquad E–=\frac{ρ}{ε_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow div.D–=ρ$

$\Rightarrow \frac{𝜕}{𝜕x}(e^{-x}\sin y)+\frac{𝜕}{𝜕y}(-e^{-x}\cos y)+\frac{𝜕}{𝜕z}(2z)=ρ$

$\Rightarrow$ $ρ$ = 2 (a constant)

V = 2 $\times$ $10^{-9} m^{3}$

q = 2 $\times$ 2 $\times$ $10^{-9} = 4 nC$

text:
The area of cross-section of a railway track is $0.01 m^{2}$. The temperature variation is 10${}^{\circ }$C. Coefficient of linear expansion of material of track is $10^{-5}/{}^{\circ }$C. The energy stored per meter in the track is $____________ J/m$.

(Young's modulus of material of track is $10^{11} Nm^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the tracks won't be allowed to expand linearly, the rise in temperature would lead to developing thermal stress in track.

$\frac{(Stress)}{y}=α\Delta T$ or $σ=Yα\Delta T$

Energy stored per unit volume = $\frac{1}{2}\frac{σ^{2}}{Y}$

$\Rightarrow$ Energy stored per unit length = $\frac{Aσ^{2}}{2Y}$

$=\frac{A}{2}\times Yα^{2}\Delta T^{2}$

$=\frac{10^{-2}\times 10^{11}\times 10^{-10}\times 100}{2}=5$ J/m
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift
